transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-22
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Ava (Redwood SE), Leo (Redwood CSM); Maya, Omar, Priya, Samir (NimbleHealth)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Jordan gave an orientation to Redwood's onboarding path for enterprise vendors. Main asks: MSA redlines, DPA clarifications, SLA target negotiation and pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted. Security wanted SOC2 and KMS details. Finance flagged committed usage and overage billing questions.

00:00 Jordan Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick roll call?
00:06 Maya Chen: Maya here, hi
00:07 Omar Reyes: Omar from procurement
00:08 Priya Kapoor: Priya, Infosec
00:09 Samir Das: Samir, finance
00:11 Jordan Patel: Great, I'll kick off, the agenda we sent was onboarding path, MSA/DPA items, pricing options and pilot scope, we'll try to leave 10 for Qs
00:22 Ava Grant: Quick technical context from our side, we typically split into Hosted API for quick pilots, Dedicated reserved pools for committed workloads, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated data, but you can mix and match
00:38 Maya Chen: For NimbleHealth we are focused on PII-sensitive summarization, so the VPC and KMS things are important, but we want to understand cost tradeoffs as well
00:50 Samir Das: On cost I'm less interested in list price, more how committed usage and burst works, like if we reserve X GPUs what happens with overage, credits, refund SLA?
01:05 Jordan Patel: Yeah totally. Our Dedicated offering supports reserved pools with autoscale and burst lanes; we offer tiered discounts for monthly/annual commitments and SLO-backed latency targets. For overage it's two options typically: bill at overage rate or allow short burst credits depending on the contract. We can propose both in the MSA.
01:35 Priya Kapoor: From security side, we need full details: where keys are stored, HSM/KMS option, whether logs contain PII, audit log retention, and whether we can route through an existing VPC connector or if a private stack is required
01:52 Ava Grant: For KMS we integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can support bringing-your-own-HSM in Private deployments. Audit logs can be exported to your S3/GCS and we have configurable retention windows; by default logs redact payloads but we'll enumerate exact fields in the DPA appendix
02:12 Omar Reyes: Legal will want the DPA specifics—data residency, subprocessor list, breach timelines—are those usually in the DPA or in SOW attachments?
02:25 Jordan Patel: Usually DPA covers residency, subprocessors, data subject rights; we attach a subprocessor list and SOC2 report via secure link. MSA will handle indemnities, liability caps, termination for convenience etc. We can accept certain standard redlines but need to review on a case-by-case basis
02:49 Samir Das: Liability caps—our counsel will push for higher caps given criticality of patient data provisioning, is that something Redwood is open to?
03:02 Jordan Patel: We have flex room on enterprise deals; often that's tied to committed spend. There is a path for elevated caps during contracting stage, we should flag that to legal early.
03:18 Priya Kapoor: Can you confirm whether model weights or telemetry could be used for training? NimbleHealth requires no training on customer data
03:28 Ava Grant: Good point. Our standard is no training on customer input for Hosted and Dedicated, and for Private deployment it's fully customer-controlled. We'll add explicit non-training clause into the DPA appendix for you
03:44 Maya Chen: On the pricing front, we're evaluating two paths: run everything in Hosted to start for speed, then move critical pipelines to Dedicated or Private. Need a clear migration pricing pathway though, otherwise finance will balk
04:02 Jordan Patel: Migration path is a common ask—our pricing worksheet will show break-even points given token volumes, concurrency, and latency SLOs. We'll model both the incremental cost of moving to Dedicated vs expected reduction per token.
04:21 Samir Das: We'll need an example calculation with our expected throughput—I'll share a sample 24hr trace post call
04:29 Maya Chen: We'll also need to know about SLA credits. If we miss latency SLOs or uptime SLO, how are credits calculated?
04:38 Jordan Patel: Standard SLA has uptime % and credits pro-rated; for latency SLOs we typically do an availability-to-latency SLA mapping in the appendix. For Dedicated we can tighten targets and offer higher credits.
04:55 Priya Kapoor: Does Redwood support SSO via SAML? Also RBAC for console access—infosec demands least privilege and audit trails
05:05 Ava Grant: Yes SAML SSO is supported, SCIM provisioning too. RBAC is role-based and we have audit logs with admin actions, plus token-level tracing in Console for request attribution
05:20 Omar Reyes: Procurement process question: what approvals do we need internally? Are there price tiers that require procurement board signoff vs PO only?
05:29 Samir Das: On our side, anything above $250k annually hits the procurement committee, lower can be signed with delegated authority. We need to know likely annual commitment range so we can plan the approval path
05:42 Jordan Patel: We'll provide a pricing band and example commitment figures so you can map to your procurement thresholds. We'll also note discounts by commitment term.
05:52 Maya Chen: A bit of a technical nuance: for prefix caching and KV cache, do you support sticky cache when routing between hosts? Concerned about cache cold starts during migration
06:05 Ava Grant: Our runtime provides continuous batching and KV caching; cached state can be migrated in Dedicated->Private patterns but there are caveats. We'll include technical appendix about cache warmup and best practices
06:23 Priya Kapoor: Regarding subprocessors, do you disclose cloud infra partners? Need to know if data leaves certain jurisdictions
06:31 Jordan Patel: We'll include a subprocessor list link. We host in major cloud regions; for data residency we can pin to a region or go Private for guaranteed on-prem options
06:44 Omar Reyes: About contracts—what's the typical lead time from signed MSA to production access? We have a target of 8 weeks if possible
06:53 Leo Martinez: Onboarding timeline varies: Hosted pilot can start in 1–2 weeks, Dedicated provisioning 4–8 weeks depending on capacity and networking (VPC peering, IP allowlists), Private/on-prem longer due to installation and compliance checks
07:15 Samir Das: If we do a pilot and then decide to commit, is there a credit or migration discount applied retroactively?
07:25 Jordan Patel: We can structure pilot credits toward committed spend in many cases; we'll outline options in the commercial term sheet
07:32 Priya Kapoor: Encryption in transit and at rest? Key rotation policy?
07:37 Ava Grant: TLS everywhere in transit, AES256 at rest. For customer-managed keys we defer rotation control to your KMS; we support automatic rotated keys if you prefer.
07:48 Maya Chen: Ok next can we walk through a sample SOW outline for pilot? Who owns what, data deletion, runbooks
07:56 Jordan Patel: Sure. Pilot SOW typically includes scope (models, endpoints), success metrics (latency, correctness tests), data handling clause, runbooks for incident response and escalation paths, timeline, and acceptance criteria. We'll send a template SOW after this call
08:18 Omar Reyes: On payment terms, do you accept net-60? Any early-payment discounts?
08:26 Jordan Patel: Standard is net-30, but terms can be negotiated for enterprise, early-pay discounts possible or invoicing cadence adjustments. Finance will discuss once procurement confirms commitment level.
08:40 Priya Kapoor: A couple of nitty-gritty legal asks: can Redwood accept a mutual NDAs, and will you sign a one-way DPA?
08:50 Jordan Patel: Yes we do mutual NDAs and we have a standard DPA, but we're open to minor redlines. We'll request that any major DPA changes are surfaced early so our legal can triage them
09:05 Samir Das: For budget planning, can you provide a 12-month forecast model with consumption tiers so we can map to headcount and margin impact?
09:14 Ava Grant: We'll produce a forecast model showing tokens, concurrency, committed discounts, and expected TCO. We'll include scenarios for migrating portions to Dedicated at break-even points
09:28 Maya Chen: Security question—how are logs redacted? You said by default—what's the exact behavior for structured PII fields?
09:38 Ava Grant: By default we mask recognized PII fields and store only metadata salient to request. For full compliance we can configure stricter redaction policies or route logs to your own store where you control retention
09:52 Priya Kapoor: We will want contract language that disallows model training and derivative model sharing; please include explicit clause
10:00 Jordan Patel: Noted, we'll include explicit non-training clause in DPA appendix
10:10 Omar Reyes: Regarding onboarding checklist, can we map approvals required and estimated time per step?
10:18 Leo Martinez: Yes, we'll provide an onboarding checklist: Legal review (2–3 weeks), Security review (1–2 weeks), Procurement (1–3 weeks depending on approvals), Infra setup (1–8 weeks dependent on Dedicated/Private). We'll include owners for each step
10:35 Maya Chen: Are there any compliance certifications beyond SOC2? ISO27001? HIPAA?
10:42 Jordan Patel: We have SOC2 Type II; for HIPAA we provide BAAs and Private deployments are the usual path. ISO27001 roadmap is ongoing, we can share current status in the security pack
10:55 Priya Kapoor: For BAAs, what's the typical negotiation friction? Any clauses that typically get pushed back?
11:04 Jordan Patel: Common negotiations are around indemnity, breach notifications timelines, and liability caps. We'll call those out in the redline guidance we send
11:18 Samir Das: Ok financially, what's the minimum commitment to get Dedicated discount?
11:25 Ava Grant: Typically discounts start at 50k/month committed, meaningful tiers at 100k+ and highest kicker for annual multi-hundred k. We'll show a sliding scale in the sheet
11:38 Maya Chen: Thinking timeline—if we wanted production safe by end of year, pilot start next week, is that feasible?
11:45 Jordan Patel: For Hosted pilot yes; Dedicated production by EOY is tight but possible if procurement and security sign quickly and we provision in parallel. We'll target pilot next week and aim for production readiness by late December if all goes well
11:58 Priya Kapoor: How will you handle data deletion requests and proof of deletion?
12:06 Ava Grant: We provide deletion APIs and can provide attestations for Private; for Hosted/Dedicated we'll provide deletion logs and confirmation artifacts via audit log exports. We'll describe process in DPA appendix
12:20 Omar Reyes: Who signs off on final pricing—should we expect account exec or sales ops?
12:27 Jordan Patel: Final commercial signoff typically done by Sales Ops with AE approval; for enterprise specials we may require director-level review. We'll call out approver paths in the quote
12:41 Maya Chen: Anything else from your side?
12:45 Priya Kapoor: No, just please share SOC2 and KMS diagrams
12:48 Samir Das: And the pricing worksheet with break-even
12:51 Jordan Patel: We'll send MSA redlines, pricing worksheet, SOC2 link, and pilot SOW template. Any preference on format for contractual redlines? Word with tracked changes?
13:02 Omar Reyes: Word tracked changes is best for procurement and legal review
13:08 Jordan Patel: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Jordan sends MSA redlines and commercial terms; Ava shares technical appendix and pricing sheet; Priya and team to schedule security deep dive; NimbleHealth to confirm pilot scope. We'll reconvene after pilots are scoped to lock timeline
13:30 Meeting end.
